newsitem.title: USA: US W.COAST SPOT GASOLINE DROPS AS BUYING DRIES UP.
newsitem.headline: US W.COAST SPOT GASOLINE DROPS AS BUYING DRIES UP.

text.p: Demand for U.S. West Coast spot gasoline fell early Friday, ending a two-week price surge as oversupplied dealers scrambled to sell off product before imports replenished supply, traders said.
An early August supply squeeze had sent gasoline prices up nearly 15-cent since the beginning of the month, prompting traders to buy barrels in order to stockpile the lucrative commodity.
But talk of increased San Francisco deliveries and a lower futures market Friday revived concerns that prices would tumble, and forced dealers that were "long," or holding excess barrels, to sell.
"There's a lack of buyers," a refinery trader said. "People don't want to take on length anymore. They will limp along until (local) production catches up."
In Los Angeles, CARB unleaded gasoline fell five cents a gallon to 70 cents, and offers were heard at 72 cents a gallon in early Friday trade, dealers said.
Traders said the prices for other refined products were unclear early Friday.
